summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (56/123)

data.turoyo: <...> Hano hedika kmamte i bardiš du ḥalwo, kmaḥatla ʕal i nuro w ksoyəm nuro taḥta, kfoyər u ḥalwawo kule, kqoləb, lo ḥarule. <...>
data.translation: <...> Er holt sacht den Milchtopf und stellt ihn aufs Feuer. Er macht Feuer darunter, an und die ganze Milch kocht über und verdampft; er kümmert sich nicht darum. <...>

rationale: Establishes the missing Infectum box for existing sense 1 with overt milk and heating context.

summary: New sense 3: (mit ʕal) heftig aufwallen, ansteigen (von Fieber, Blut oder Blutdruck)

data.gloss: (mit ʕal) heftig aufwallen, ansteigen (von Fieber, Blut oder Blutdruck)

rationale: The first account has intense impersonal Fuyarwo aʕle followed by doctors and recovery; the second explicitly names blood pressure/blood as subject with the same affected-person frame. Distinct from evaporation and speech-raging; no diagnosis implied.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (56/123)

data.turoyo: <...> Kroṯəḥ u ḥalwo w malik ava kale ksoyəm nuro ṭahṭe, u ḥalwo kqoləb, fayər kule, yaqiḏo i bardiš.
data.translation: <...> Die Milch kocht und er - möge dein Haus gedeihen! - macht Feuer darunter; er paßt nicht auf, die ganze Milch verdampft, der Kochtopf brennt an.

rationale: Fills Preterit Intransitive 1 with a completed total-evaporation result, contrasting kfoyər in the same verse.

data.translation: Uncle Isho: He had a very high fever.

rationale: First Infectum-wa 3; the degree phrase and medical sequel support feverish surging. Supplied English is project machine translation.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 2.7/1877)

data.translation: His blood pressure surged upon him.

rationale: First Preterit Intransitive 3; explicit blood-pressure subject and ʕal affected person make the construction clear.

summary: The two milk forms at 56/123 distinguish ongoing kfoyər from resultant fayər kule after continued heating. Both fit existing sense 1 verdampfen; boiling and overflowing are supplied by neighboring predicates and do not warrant a new sense.
The speech-domain fuyarwo at 11/266 is the inherited sense 2 rasen in Infectum-wa. No evidence requires reassignment to fyr 1 'fly'.
No new collocation or Detransitive function is established.
fyr-2 is identified from boiling/raging semantics and the inherited Arabic etymology; none of these contexts supports the flying homonym.
No stroke, hypertension episode or specific fatal mechanism is inferred from the folk-medical account. The contrast with poisoning is reported speech.
Round-1 evaporation additions remain baseline and are not repeated. The new bodily construction is illustrated once per attested box, rather than once per repeated clause.
In 56/123, can fyr itself include boiling over, or is evaporation the core meaning while kqoləb expresses overflowing? The current gloss is retained pending lexical evidence.
Is impersonal Fuyarwo aʕle a conventional fever expression, and what range of bodily processes can fyr describe with ṭansiyon/admo? A clinical diagnosis is not proposed.
In Jan 2.13/3359, did the flour sack overflow, swell, replenish itself or lose contents? Resolve the miracle account before publishing a new lexical sense.
Fever account has an implicit heat/cause with aʕle, while the blood-pressure account has an overt subject. These are two contexts for the same physiological surging construction.
